Step 1 – Compound A  
Propionaldehyde (CH₃–CH₂–CHO) reacts with 1,2-ethanedithiol (EDT) in the presence of BF₃ to give the 1,3-dithiolane (thio­acetal)  

  A = 2-ethyl-1,3-dithiolane  

(the former carbonyl carbon becomes the C-2 of the ring and bears an ethyl group and one H).

Step 2 – Compound B  
Treatment of A with BuLi removes the acidic H at C-2 (between the two S atoms) to give the corresponding lithium carbanion  

  B = 2-ethyl-2-lithio-1,3-dithiolane.

Step 3 – Compound C  
Alkylation of that carbanion with bromoethane introduces a second ethyl group at C-2:  

  C = 2,2-diethyl-1,3-dithiolane.

Step 4 – Compound D  
Desulfurisation of the dithiolane with HgCl₂/H₂O/H⁺ regenerates the carbonyl, so C is converted into the corresponding ketone:  

  D = (CH₃CH₂)₂C=O  i.e. pentan-3-one (diethyl ketone).

Step 5 – Compound E  
PPh₃ reacts with 3-bromopentane to give the phosphonium salt, which BuLi deprotonates to the ylide (C₂H₅)₂C=PPh₃.  
Wittig reaction of this ylide with ketone D couples two (C₂H₅)₂C= fragments to give the tetrasubstituted alkene  

  E = (C₂H₅)₂C=C(C₂H₅)₂    (i.e. tetra-ethyl­ethene).

Structure of E  
  CH₃CH₂–       CH₂CH₃  
    \       /  
     C = C  
    /       \  
  CH₃CH₂–       CH₂CH₃

Symmetry and ¹³C-NMR signals for E  
The molecule possesses a C₂ (and mirror) symmetry that exchanges the two olefinic carbons as well as all four ethyl substituents.  
• Olefinic carbons: both are equivalent → 1 signal  
• α-Carbons of all ethyl groups (the CH₂’s attached directly to the double bond) are equivalent → 1 signal  
• Terminal methyl carbons of all ethyl groups are equivalent → 1 signal  

Total distinct ¹³C-NMR signals = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

Answer: C
